quote_zh: To a clean and pre-dried 250mL round bottomed flask, dichloromethane (100mL) NMSBA (25g, 0.10mol) and 1, 3-cyclohexanedione (12g, 0.11mol) were added under stirring at the temperature of 25-30°C. To this mixture, N,N’-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide(DCC) (21g, 0.10mol) was added and stirred for about 2 hours at 25-30°C. The reaction mixture was filtered under vacuum to obtain the wet cake. The wet cake is dried to obtain the crude enol ester. The crude enol ester with water was filtered under vacuum to obtain pure enol ester as off white colour solid. HPLC purity > 85%; Yield: 22.8g (66%). Melting point 157-163°C and Solvent recovery >85%.
arithmetic_check:
THREE MASS/MOLE PAIRS, ONE PRODUCT MASS AND ONE PRINTED YIELD. Molecular weights computed with RDKit from the structures the document draws for these compounds elsewhere: NMSBA C8H7NO6S = 245.212 g/mol, 1,3-cyclohexanedione C6H8O2 = 112.128 g/mol, N,N’-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide C13H22N2 = 206.333 g/mol, enol ester of formula (II) C14H13NO7S = 339.325 g/mol.

ALL THREE INPUT PAIRS CLOSE at the precision at which the patent prints the moles, so molar_mass_inconsistent is NOT raised. NMSBA: 25 g / 245.212 = 0.101953 mol, which rounds at two decimal places to the printed 0.10 mol; the printed pair 25 g / 0.10 mol would imply 250 g/mol, but the rounding window of 0.10 mol (0.095 to 0.105 mol) implies 238.1 to 263.2 g/mol and 245.212 lies inside it. Dione: 12 g / 112.128 = 0.107021 mol, which rounds to the printed 0.11 mol. DCC: 21 g / 206.333 = 0.101777 mol, which rounds to the printed 0.10 mol. So every printed mole figure is the printed mass divided by the correct molecular weight and then rounded to two decimals, and no pair is inconsistent with the compound named.

THE PRINTED YIELD IS 66% AND THE MASSES RECOMPUTE TO EITHER 67.2% OR 65.9% DEPENDING ON THE BASIS, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. On the ROUNDED MOLE BASIS: theoretical = 0.10 mol x 339.325 = 33.9325 g, and 22.8 / 33.9325 = 67.19%, about one point above the printed 66%. On the PRINTED MASS BASIS: theoretical = (25 / 245.212) x 339.325 = 34.5951 g, and 22.8 / 34.5951 = 65.91%, which rounds to exactly the printed 66%. The patent's own figure is therefore correct on its own charge mass, and the apparent one-point gap is produced entirely by reading the theoretical off the mole figure the patent rounded down to 0.10 rather than off the 25 g it actually weighed. Read the other way, 66% of 33.9325 g would be 22.40 g against the 22.8 g printed, a difference of 0.4 g, which is the same rounding seen from the mass side.

WHAT WAS RECORDED. product_yield_pct is 66.0, the PRINTED value, and mass_g is 22.8, the PRINTED value. Neither was adjusted and no recomputed percentage was written into reactions.json; the 67.19 and 65.91 figures above appear NOWHERE in the patent and exist only in this sidecar, which is the field the pass provides for a recomputation. A1 handled the same numbers the same way, recording yield_pct 66.0 with the recomputation labelled as a recomputation in its notes, so A1 and A2 agree on the printed fact and on which figure is the patent's.

mass_balance_implausible NOT RAISED, by arithmetic and not by expectation. The two limbs of the check both pass. The stated product mass does not exceed what the stated input moles could give: 22.8 g against a theoretical of 33.9325 g on the rounded basis or 34.5951 g on the mass basis, so there is no mass appearing from nowhere. And the stated mass and the stated yield do not disagree: they agree to the printed rounding once the theoretical is taken from the printed charge mass, as shown above. CONTROL, Example 4, the same transformation at a nearby scale: 27 g NMSBA (printed 0.11 mol; 27 / 245.212 = 0.110109 mol, closes), 25.4 g product, printed 68%, and the recomputation gives 68.05% on the rounded mole basis and 67.98% on the mass basis, both rounding to the printed 68%. So this transformation's arithmetic closes on both bases in the neighbouring example, and Example 6's slightly wider spread is a rounding artefact of a 25 g charge whose mole figure lost precision, not a defect. For completeness, Example 5 at 1.0 g prints 65% where 0.89 g recomputes to 65.57% on the rounded basis and 64.32% on the mass basis; that is Example 5's business, not this record's, and is noted only to show that the printed percentages in this family are rounded rather than exact.

STOICHIOMETRY, computed here and deliberately NOT written into the record because the patent states no equivalents and prints no molar ratio: on the printed 0.10 mol of NMSBA the dione is 1.10 eq and the carbodiimide 1.00 eq; on the mass-derived 0.101953 mol the dione is 1.05 eq and the carbodiimide 1.00 eq. The dione is the charge held in slight excess on either reading. molar_ratio_text is null because the text words no ratio.

NO SCALE-CONTINUITY TEST IS POSSIBLE. NMSBA is made by earlier examples of this patent, but this section names no batch, example or lot for the 25 g it charges, so there is no stated previous output to compare against and scale_discontinuity would be asserting a continuity the page never claims. It is not raised, and precursor_step is left null rather than pointing at one of the three earlier examples that each make NMSBA.

PURITY IS A MEASUREMENT REPORTED AS A BOUND, NOT A SPECIFICATION. The unmarked line 318 prints "HPLC purity > 85%" for the single batch this example made, so product_purity_pct is 85.0 with purity_method hplc, the inequality kept verbatim in quote_zh, procedure_text and the record notes, and 85.0 understood as that printed lower bound rather than an assayed equality. This agrees with A1, which holds purity_pct 85.0 and raw_text "HPLC purity > 85%" for the same compound. The summary section's "at least 65%" and "at least 85%" are specifications of the invention in general, are not measurements, and are recorded in no numeric field.

SOLVENT RECOVERY IS NOT A NUMBER ON THIS RECORD. The same line prints "Solvent recovery >85%", which can only mean the dichloromethane. It is not product_purity_pct, not any compound's purity_pct and not an analytics entry on the product, because it is a property of the solvent and not of the product; and it is not byproduct_recovery, because the dichloromethane is the reaction solvent rather than a by-product AND because the written procedure isolates the product by two vacuum filtrations and never describes distilling, condensing, drying or reusing the solvent, so there is no recovery operation in the text for that field to describe. It is recorded as an observation about what the page states, which is how Pass V and A1 both recorded it, and not as a contradiction of the procedure. No flag is raised on it: it is a statement the page makes that the procedure does not support, which is worth recording and is not an arithmetic or an extraction defect.

MELTING POINT. "Melting point 157-163°C" is printed and has no field on the reaction record; it lives on the A1 compound, which carries min 157.0 and max 163.0. Cross-checked only for plausibility against the same compound in the neighbouring examples (158-163°C in Example 4, 152-158°C in Example 5), which overlap; nothing was harmonised.

DICYCLOHEXYLUREA. The co-product of a carbodiimide coupling is not named anywhere in this section and no mass is printed for the wet cake, so no by-product record and no by-product mass balance was attempted. Had the cake been weighed, the urea at 224.348 g/mol would have been the figure to test against, and it was not.
drawing_evidence:
NO DRAWING EVIDENCE EXISTS FOR THIS STEP, and that is a finding rather than a gap. There is NO [IMAGE_EXTRACT: ...] span of any kind inside lines 312-319: the section is a title line, a sub-title line, the marked paragraph [0052] and the unmarked analytical line, with their byte-identical "> EN:" duplicates, and nothing else. Every reagent, the solvent, the temperature range and the time in this record therefore come from the prose of lines 316 and 318, and nothing was imported from a scheme or from a neighbouring example.

WHAT THE NEAREST SPANS ARE, AND WHY THEY ARE NOT MINE. The closest scheme span is at line 287, which draws exactly this transformation (reactants C8H7NO6S and C6H8O2, product C14H13NO7S, conditions list EMPTY) but is printed inside Example 3's line range and belongs to Example 4, which is a known mis-anchoring by build_enriched.py from its between_markers. Examples 4, 5 and 6 all run the same coupling and only Example 4's arrow is drawn; Example 6 owns no arrow. Attributing line 287 to this record would be borrowing another section's drawing, so it was not used as evidence for anything here, not for connectivity, not for reagents and not for conditions.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FLAGS. drawing_text_conflict, reagent_drawn_not_written, reagent_written_not_drawn and route_attribution_unclear are all left UNRAISED, because each asserts a relation between a drawn arrow and a written procedure and this section has no drawn arrow to stand on either side of that relation. This is not a guard passing on absence: the absence is the reported fact, stated here and in the record notes, rather than an unchecked condition reported as clean. Worth recording separately: the one arrow that does draw this transformation, at line 287, carries an EMPTY conditions list, so even the borrowed drawing would have contributed no reagent, no solvent and no condition, and the prose would still have been the only source. That matches the pattern across the invention's schemes for steps (ii) and (iii), which are drawn bare.

ROUTE ATTRIBUTION IS NOT IN QUESTION. This is an Example under the EXAMPLES heading of the specification, so it is the invention's own route, and no scheme needed to be attributed. NMSBC, the acid chloride of the four-step prior art of US 7,820,863, appears NOWHERE in lines 312-319 and is a reactant or product of nothing on this record: the acid couples directly, which is the inventive point of step (ii).

PRODUCT IDENTITY WITHOUT A DRAWING. The section never gives the product a chemical name, only the class term and its formula number, so product_name is the A1 identifier "enol ester of formula (II)", taken verbatim from A1 and matching the title line 314. It is the flattened identifier of the one compound with is_product true, not a coined description, and "crude enol ester" and "pure enol ester" are the same material at two points of the work-up and are A1 aliases rather than separate products. No SMILES was written on any field of this record.
